newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures post sharp losses in short day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures post sharp losses in short day.

text.p: U.S. debt futures posed sharp losses in a shortened holiday session, pressured by strong housing data earlier in the day.
Traders said much faster than expected growth in new home sales in November sparked nervousness in thin trading pits ahead of other key data later this week.
New home sales rose 14.2 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 772,000 after a downward-revised 676,000 in October.
Chicago's purchasing managers overall index and December consumer confidence were also slightly stronger than forecast.
"People are a little bit nervous now with NAPM and the employment report coming up," a T-bond futures trader said.
The December national purchasing management report will be released Thursday at 0900 CST/1500 GMT, and was forecast at 52.3 from 52.7 in the previous report.
The December jobs report will be released on Friday, January 10.
"Those numbers (released Tuesday) are pretty disturbing," the trader said. "There's got to be some concern before the payrolls numbers."
Chicago's NAPM fell to 57.4 from 57.6 in November, but was higher than the 55.6 forecast.
December consumer confidence rose to 113.8 from a revised 109.5 in November, the Conference Board reported.
Early in the session, New York's December NAPM index was reported up to 72.9 from 64.9 in November.
IMM Eurodollars ended 10 minutes before bond futures closed and overall Euro volume was estimated at 195,000 contracts.
"That's decent volume for a shortened session, but we didn't see much and flows were light off the desk," a broker said.
March Euros posted a double bottom at the one-week low of 94.43, but trade was very quiet after the initial selloff.
There is no trade Wednesday, January 1, in T-bonds and Euros in observance of the New Year's holiday.
March T-bonds registered the lowest price since the two-month low at 111-27/32 set on December 19. Support now was seen at 112-02/32, the two-month low settlement from December 18.

At settlement, March T-bonds were off 1-8/32 points to 112-20/32, March 10-year notes were down 25/32 to 109-4/32, Five-year notes lost 15/32 to 106-19/32, munis fell 1-4/32 points to 116-2/32, March Euros ended down three basis points to 94.44 and June Euros lost five to 94.28.
